Mission_Objective: Make the doctor aware of what is safe, what is risky, and what is strictly unsafe on Google Business Profile before any setup begins.
Brief_Description: A categorized reference of GBP actions: safe (routine management), risky (triggers re-verification or review), and unsafe (triggers suspension or listing removal). Covers why the business name, address, phone number, and category are the highest-risk fields once set, and why they should not be casually changed.
Step_By_Step_Guide:
🟢 SAFE — routine, does not alter core identity anchors: uploading real clinic photos/videos, publishing Google Posts, responding to reviews, updating hours for holidays, adding/editing attributes and description within reason.

🟡 RISKY — can trigger re-verification or review: changing business name (even minor wording), changing address (even a suite/floor change), changing primary category, adding/removing multiple categories at once, changing phone number.

🔴 UNSAFE — can trigger suspension or listing removal: using a name that doesn't match your signage, using virtual/tracking phone numbers, creating a duplicate listing for the same practice, keyword-stuffing the business name (e.g. 'Best ENT Doctor'), operating from an address that doesn't match a real, staffed location.

Read this before touching any field below. Name, address, phone, and category are the four fields you get, essentially, one real chance to set correctly.
Success_Message: You now know which fields are safe to edit freely and which ones require getting it right the first time.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: A simple acknowledgement checkbox/confirmation, stored against the doctor's account.
input_1: Acknowledgement: I have read and understood the risks of suspension and re-verification

Mission_Objective: Set the GBP business name correctly the first time, since it is a locked, high-risk field.
Brief_Description: Your business name on GBP must match your real-world signage exactly. It cannot contain descriptors, credentials, or superlatives (no 'Dr.', no 'Best', no 'Top', no specialty tacked on) per Google's guidelines — those belong in the category and description fields, not the name. Changing this later risks re-verification or suspension.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Why this matters: Google verifies your name against your real signage and public presence. A mismatch, or a name that reads as keyword-stuffed, is one of the most common causes of suspension. Enter your business name exactly as it appears on your clinic signage. AI will check it against common violations (superlatives, credentials, keyword-stuffing) and flag anything risky before you lock it in.
Prompt_output_with_placeholder: Review the doctor's entered business name: {{clinic_name}}. Check it does not contain superlatives ('best', 'top', 'no.1'), credentials ('Dr.', 'MD', 'MS'), or specialty keywords stuffed into the name. If clean, confirm: 'This name is safe to use as your GBP Business Name.' If it contains a flagged pattern, explain specifically which part is risky and why, and suggest the corrected version using only the real, signage-matching business name.
Success_Message: Your business name is confirmed safe to use for your GBP listing.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Doctor enters their business name; AI checks it against name-related suspension risks and confirms or flags before it's used.
input_1: Business name (as it appears on clinic signage)

Mission_Objective: Confirm the practice address correctly, since it is a locked, high-risk field once verified.
Brief_Description: Your GBP address must be a real, staffed location matching your public presence. Address is auto-pulled from your profile section — confirm it is accurate before it's used to create or verify your GBP listing.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Why this matters: an address mismatch, or an address that doesn't correspond to a real staffed location, is a direct suspension trigger. Google may also send a physical postcard or require video verification tied to this exact address. Your address has been pulled from your profile: {{clinic_address}}, {{city}}, {{state}}, {{pin_code}}. Confirm this is accurate and current before proceeding.
Success_Message: Your address is confirmed and ready to use for GBP setup.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Address is auto-populated from the doctor's profile section; doctor confirms accuracy, no re-typing required.
input_1: Confirm address pulled from profile is accurate

Mission_Objective: Confirm the practice's appointment phone number correctly, since it is a locked, high-risk field once verified.
Brief_Description: Your GBP phone number must be a real, direct number for your practice — never a virtual or call-tracking number. Phone number is auto-pulled from your profile section. Changing it after verification is one of the more common causes of suspension.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Why this matters: Google cross-checks your phone number against public directories and your own website. A virtual number, a number that changes, or a mismatch with what's published elsewhere is a real suspension risk. Your appointment number has been pulled from your profile: {{appointment_number}}. Confirm this is a real, direct, permanent number for your practice before proceeding.
Success_Message: Your phone number is confirmed and ready to use for GBP setup.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Phone number is auto-populated from the doctor's profile section; doctor confirms accuracy, no re-typing required.
input_1: Confirm phone number pulled from profile is accurate and not a virtual number

Mission_Objective: Set the single most accurate primary GBP category — the field most doctors get wrong, and the one hardest to safely correct later.
Brief_Description: AI suggests the most accurate primary category based on your specialty and profile, before you touch GBP. Setting the right primary category the first time avoids a later re-verification risk.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Why this matters: your primary category is the single strongest signal Google uses to decide which searches you show up for. Getting it wrong, then changing it later, is a real re-verification/suspension risk — so get it right now. Below is an AI-suggested primary category based on your specialty. Review it, confirm or adjust, then set it in GBP: Edit Profile → Business Category.
Prompt_output_with_placeholder: Based on the doctor's specialty ({{specialty}}) and subspecialty ({{subspecialty}}), suggest the single MOST ACCURATE Google Business Profile primary category available in Google's official category list. Do NOT suggest a category that is broader or narrower than what actually, precisely describes this doctor's core practice. OUTPUT: one recommended primary category, with a one-line reason why it's the best fit, for the doctor to confirm or override before setting it in GBP.
Success_Message: Your primary category is confirmed and ready to set in GBP.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: AI suggests the primary category from the doctor's specialty; doctor confirms or overrides before setting it live in GBP.
input_1: Confirm or override the AI-suggested primary category

Mission_Objective: Create the Google Business Profile account itself using the confirmed name, address, phone, and primary category.
Brief_Description: With name, address, phone and primary category all confirmed in the steps above, create the GBP listing. No re-entry needed — everything below is pulled from what's already confirmed.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Sign in with your DEDICATED clinic Google account — remember this exact account, you'll reuse it to connect Gemini next. Enter the confirmed business name, address, phone, and category. When Google asks to verify, choose the offered method (often video verification for medical practices). Do not use a personal or shared account — this account is the permanent identity of your GBP listing.
Success_Message: Your GBP account has been created and submitted for verification.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Doctor creates the account using only the already-confirmed name/address/phone/category — no new decisions at this step.
input_1: Confirm GBP account created with the exact confirmed details

Mission_Objective: Research what categories real competitors are using before adding any subcategories — subcategory choice should be evidence-based, not guessed.
Brief_Description: Look up 3-5 real competing practices in your city and specialty on Google Maps. Note their listed categories. This becomes the input for the AI-suggested subcategories in the next step.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Search Google Maps for your specialty + city (e.g. '{{specialty}} in {{city}}'). Open 3-5 competing listings. Note down every category each one has listed (visible under their business name on their GBP page). You are not copying them — you are gathering real, in-use categories relevant to your field, to inform your own subcategory choices.
Success_Message: Competitor category research complete — ready to select your own subcategories.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Doctor manually researches and lists real competitor categories; this list feeds directly into the next mission.
input_1: List of categories observed across 3-5 competitor listings

Mission_Objective: Add a lean, genuinely relevant set of secondary categories, informed by real competitor research, not guesswork or stuffing.
Brief_Description: Using the competitor categories you just researched, AI suggests a lean set of 3-6 secondary categories that genuinely apply to your practice. Do not stuff categories — irrelevant ones dilute relevance rather than helping it.
Step_By_Step_Guide: This CAN be edited later without the same suspension risk as your primary category, but keep it lean. Do NOT add every category you saw a competitor use — only the ones that are genuinely, specifically true of your practice.
Prompt_output_with_placeholder: Using the doctor's competitor category research: {{competitor_categories_observed}}, and the doctor's specialty {{specialty}} ({{subspecialty}}) in {{city}}, suggest a LEAN set of 3 to 6 genuinely relevant secondary categories — only ones that truly apply to this specific practice, not a broad or padded list. OUTPUT: 3 to 6 recommended secondary categories with a one-line reason each, for the doctor to confirm, edit, or remove before setting them in GBP.
Success_Message: Your secondary categories are confirmed and ready to set in GBP.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: AI suggests secondary categories from real competitor research; doctor confirms the final lean set before publishing.
input_1: Confirm, edit, or remove each AI-suggested secondary category

Mission_Objective: Connect the doctor's GBP account to Gemini so future optimization tasks (description, attributes, and beyond) can be done through a single chat interface.
Brief_Description: The email that owns your GBP and the email you use in Gemini must be the SAME clinic account. This connection is what allows every future task in this program to be done via a simple chat instruction rather than digging through GBP's own interface.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Confirm you have OWNER access on the GBP profile (not just manager). If someone else set it up, transfer ownership to your clinic account first. Sign in to Gemini with that same clinic Google account. In the Gemini chat box, type '@' and choose 'Google Business Profile' from the list — this creates a business notebook. Gemini will prompt you to connect and confirm the profile. Once connected, every remaining setup step below can be done directly through this chat.
Success_Message: Your GBP is now connected to Gemini. All remaining setup steps can be done through this chat.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: One-time connection step; doctor confirms the same clinic email owns both GBP and the Gemini session.
input_1: Confirm Gemini successfully connected to the correct GBP account

Mission_Objective: Write a compliant, non-stuffed, non-promotional GBP description using your full profile context.
Brief_Description: AI writes the description using your specialty, city, diseases treated, procedures, and areas of expertise/interest already on file — you don't re-type any of it. Description must read naturally, stay under 750 characters, and contain no superlatives or promotional claims.
Step_By_Step_Guide: Read the AI output. Confirm it reads naturally (not keyword-stuffed), stays under 750 characters, and contains no superlatives ('best', 'leading', 'top') or promotional claims. In GBP (or via Gemini), go to Edit Profile → Description and paste it in. Save.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: AI generates the description from existing profile data; doctor reviews and publishes via GBP or Gemini.
input_1: Approve or edit the AI-generated description before publishing
input_2: Confirm published text is under 750 characters with no superlatives

Mission_Objective: Select accurate practice attributes and set consultation timings — both editable freely, low risk.
Brief_Description: Select attributes that genuinely apply to your practice (accessibility, amenities, appointment/referral requirements, payment options) and set your consultation hours accurately.
Step_By_Step_Guide: These fields are low-risk and can be edited via Gemini-GBP chat going forward. Select only attributes that are genuinely true of your practice — accessibility (wheelchair access, parking), amenities (restroom, Wi-Fi), planning (appointment required, accepts new patients), payment options. Set consultation hours to match your actual, current timings.
Success_Message: Your attributes and timings are set and published.
Mission_inputs_from_doctor: Doctor selects genuinely-applicable attributes and confirms timings; low-risk, freely editable going forward.
input_2: Confirm consultation timings are current and accurate
